'''Richard Francis Xavier Casten''' (born November 1, 1941) is an American [[Nuclear physics|nuclear physicist]] known for his research in [[nuclear structure]] and radioactive [[Nuclear pumped laser|nuclear beams]].  He is the D. Allan Bromley Professor Emeritus of Physics at [[Yale University]], where he was the director of the Wright Nuclear Structure Laboratory from 1995 to 2008.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Laurans |first=Penelope |year=2015 |title=Richard F. Casten |url=https://fas.yale.edu/book/faculty-retirement-tributes-2015/richard-f-casten |access-date=2023-11-27 |website=Faculty of Arts and Sciences |publisher=[[Yale University]]}}</ref> He is also known for Casten's triangle, which was introduced in 1981.<ref>{{cite book | title = The Interacting Boson Model| isbn = 978-0-521-30282-1 | author1 = Iachello, F | author-link=Francesco Iachello |author2 = Arima, A. |author-link2=Akito Arima | date = 2006-11-02 | pages=81–84 | publisher = Cambridge University Press | url=https://books.google.com/books?id=PXv_SRqDG_IC&pg=PA81}}</ref>

== Early life and education <!--Note: Some of these citations apply also to other sentences in their respective section, especially preceding ones.--> ==
Casten was born on November 1, 1941, in [[New York City]].<ref name="aip" /> His father was a [[Jews|Jewish]] surgeon from [[New York (state)|New York]] and his mother was a Catholic [[homemaker]]. Casten was raised in [[Manhattan]] and attended the Quaker [[Friends Seminary]], where he took chemistry classes and decided to pursue physics.<ref name="Zierler">{{cite web |last=Zierler |first=David |date=June 25, 2020 |title=Interview of Richard Casten |url=https://www.aip.org/history-programs/niels-bohr-library/oral-histories/46761 |access-date=November 27, 2023 |website=Niels Bohr Library & Archives |publisher=[[American Institute of Physics]]}}</ref>

Casten graduated from the [[College of the Holy Cross]] with a [[Bachelor of Science]] in physics, ''[[magna cum laude]]'', in 1963.<ref name=":1">{{Cite news |orig-date=February 1964 |title=Degrees in Course: Bachelor of Science Honors Magna Cum Laude |volume=60 |work=Catalogue |publisher=[[College of the Holy Cross]] |location=[[Worcester, Massachusetts]] |url=https://crossworks.holycross.edu/cgi/viewcontent.cgi?article=1090&context=course_catalog|pages=127, 145}}</ref> As an undergraduate at Holy Cross, he was elected to [[Delta Epsilon Sigma]] and was a member of its honors program.<ref name=":1" /> The college's focus on a [[liberal arts education]] allowed him to take courses in history and philosophy, which he later recalled as having "an effect on my whole research career".<ref name="Zierler" /> 

After graduation, Casten pursued graduate studies at [[Yale University]], where he studied [[Coulomb excitation]] in [[osmium isotope]]s under the direction of physicist [[D. Allan Bromley]].<ref name="Zierler" /> He earned his [[Master of Science]] (M.S.) in physics from Yale in 1964 and his [[Ph.D.]] in physics from Yale in 1967.<ref name="aip">{{cite web |title=R. Casten, Biography {{!}} Physics History Network |url=https://history.aip.org/phn/11502018.html |access-date=November 27, 2023 |website=[[American Institute of Physics]]}}</ref> Casten had begun his dissertation in September 1963 and completed his [[thesis defense]] in August 1967; his doctoral committee included Bromley, Jack Greenberg, and [[Charles K. Bockelman]].<ref name="Zierler" /><ref>{{cite journal|author=Gai, Moshe|author2=Hirshfield, Jay L.|author3=Sandweiss, Jack|title=Obituary. Jack Sam Greenberg|date=October 2005|journal=Physics Today|volume=58|issue=10|pages=99–100|doi=10.1063/1.2138436|doi-access=free}}</ref> His doctoral dissertation, ''Collective Nuclear Structure Studies in the Osmium Nuclei'', was the first thesis to be based upon research done with Yale's MP-1 [[tandem accelerator]].<ref name="BonnerPrize">{{cite web |date=2011 |title=2011 Tom W. Bonner Prize in Nuclear Physics Recipient – Richard F. Casten, Yale University |url=https://www.aps.org/programs/honors/prizes/prizerecipient.cfm?last_nm=Casten&first_nm=Richard&year=2011 |access-date=November 27, 2023 |website=[[American Physical Society]]}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last1=Qi |first1=Andrew |last2=Cao |first2=Carrie |date=March 29, 2015 |title=Rebirth of Wright |url=https://www.yalescientific.org/2015/03/rebirth-of-wright/ |access-date=2023-11-28 |website=[[Yale Scientific Magazine]] |publisher=[[Yale University]]}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|author=Wegner, H. E.|author2=Thieberger, P.|year=1977|title=North-American MP tandem accelerators|journal=Revue de Physique Appliquée|volume=12|issue=10|pages=1291–1301|doi=10.1051/rphysap:0197700120100129100 |url=https://www.researchgate.net/publication/46155731}}</ref>

== Career <!--Note: Some of these citations apply also to other sentences in their respective section, especially preceding ones.--> ==
From 1967 to 1969, Casten was a [[postdoctoral research fellow]] at the [[Niels Bohr Institute]] of the [[University of Copenhagen]].<ref name="DNS2005">{{Cite news |last=Gibson |first=Benjamin F. |date=November 2005 |title=Candidate Biographies {{!}} Nominations for Vice-Chair |page=5 |work=Division of Nuclear Physics |publisher=[[The American Physical Society]] |issue=145 |url=https://higherlogicdownload.s3.amazonaws.com/APS/9487474c-539c-4417-81e5-51aeb25847a8/UploadedImages/Documents/145.pdf}}</ref> He was drawn to the institute due to his research in [[Collective effects (accelerator physics)|collective effects]], and the two leading scientists of the field were [[Aage Bohr]] and [[Ben Roy Mottelson|Ben Mottelson]], who were based there; Bohr and Mottelson would later win the [[Nobel Prize in Physics]]. In addition, the Niels Bohr Institute also housed Russian physicist [[Vilen Strutinsky]]. Casten learned Danish while in Denmark and recalled his research at the institute as being on "single particle, individual nucleon behavior".<ref name="Zierler" />

Casten went to the [[Los Alamos National Laboratory]] (LANL) for additional postdoctoral research from 1969 to 1971. Thereafter, he became a physicist at the Nuclear Structure Group of the [[Brookhaven National Laboratory]] from 1971 to 1981, then a senior scientist from 1981 to 1997.<ref name="aip" /> Casten was the group leader of the Nuclear Structure Group from 1981 to 1996.<ref name="DNS2005" /> In 1995, he assumed a position as the director of the A. W. Wright Nuclear Structure Laboratory (WNSL) at Yale University and was made a professor of physics that same year.<ref name="aip" /><ref name="Zierler" /> He stepped down as director of the laboratory in 2008.<ref name="BonnerPrize" /> In the summer of 2011, WNSL's accelerator was shut down.<ref>{{cite news |date=Fall 2015 |title=The New Yale Wright Laboratory |pages=11–13 |newspaper=Physic News, Yale University |url=https://physics.yale.edu/sites/default/files/files/YalePhysics2015.pdf}}</ref>

Casten was a full professor at Yale until 2008, when he received the appointment as the university's D. Allan Bromley Professor of Physics. He served in that capacity until 2015, when he retired with [[Professor Emeritus|''emeritus'']] status.<ref name="aip" /><ref>{{cite news |last=Tipton |first=Paul |date=Fall 2015 |title=Rick Casten retires, July 2015 |page=20 |newspaper=Physics News |publisher=[[Yale University]] |url=https://physics.yale.edu/sites/default/files/files/YalePhysics2015.pdf|author-link=Paul Tipton (physicist)}}</ref> As a professor, Casten taught graduate courses in introductory and advanced nuclear physics, and an undergraduate course for non-science majors entitled Physics in the World Around Us. He authored a textbook "Nuclear Structure from a Simple Perspective" (Oxford University Press, 1990, 2000)<ref>{{Cite news |date=Summer 2001 |title=Faculty News for 2000-2001 {{!}} Richard Casten |page=7 |work=Yale Department of Physics Newsletter |publisher=[[Yale University]] |url=https://physics.yale.edu/sites/default/files/files/2001-Summer_YalePhysics.pdf |access-date=November 28, 2023}}</ref> He has been an associate editor for ''[[Physical Review C]]'' for experimental nuclear structure. He held visiting positions at the [[Institut Laue–Langevin]], at the [[University of Cologne]]'s Institute for Nuclear Physics, at the [[CERN]]/[[ISOLDE]] facility,<ref name="BonnerPrize" /> and at [[Stony Brook University]].<ref name=":0">{{cite news |date=March 3, 2006 |title=Richard Casten is named D. Allan Bromley Professor |volume=34 |newspaper=Yale Bulletin & Calendar |publisher=[[Yale University]] |issue=21 |url=http://www.yale.edu/opa/arc-ybc/v34.n21/story8.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090418132705/http://www.yale.edu/opa/arc-ybc/v34.n21/story8.html |archive-date=18 April 2009}}</ref> He chaired the [[United States Department of Energy]]'s and [[National Science Foundation]]'s Nuclear Science Advisory Committee (NSAC) from 2003 to 2005, and served on four NSAC Long Range Planning Groups. He was chair of the [[American Physical Society]]'s Division of Nuclear Physics (DNP) in 2008, and of several Steering Committees for an advanced exotic beam facility from 1989 through 2009 and of the [[FRIB]] Science Advisory Committee from 2009 to 2012.<ref name="BonnerPrize" />

== Awards and honors ==
Casten was elected in 1981 to be a fellow of the [[American Physical Society]] (APS).<ref>{{cite web |title=APS Fellow Archive |url=https://www.aps.org/programs/honors/fellowships/archive-all.cfm?initial=&year=1981&unit_id=Brookhaven+National+Laboratory |website=[[American Physical Society]]}} (search on year=1981 and institution=Brookhaven National Laboratory)</ref> In 1987, he was elected to be a fellow of the [[American Association for the Advancement of Science]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.aaas.org/fellows/historic|title=Historic Fellows Listing| website=American Association for the Advancement of Science}} (search on last name "Casten")</ref> In 1983, he received a [[Humboldt Research Award|Humboldt Award for Senior U.S. Scientists]]. He was awarded [[honorary doctorate]]s by the [[University of Bucharest]] and the [[University of Surrey]].<ref name=BonnerPrize/>

In 2009, Casten received the Mentoring Award from the Nuclear Physics Section of the APS for "his outstanding commitment to mentoring women in nuclear science and preparing them for leadership roles".<ref>{{cite web |date=November 2, 2009 |title=Richard Casten (D. Allan Bromley Professor of Physics) was recently presented with the 2009 Mentoring Award by the Division of Nuclear Physics of the American Physical Society |url=https://physics.yale.edu/news/richard-casten-d-allan-bromley-professor-physics-was-recently-presented-2009-mentoring-award |access-date=November 28, 2023 |website=Department of Physics |publisher=[[Yale University]]}}</ref>  In 2011, he received the [[Tom W. Bonner Prize in Nuclear Physics]] "for providing critical insight into the evolution of nuclear structure with varying proton and neutron numbers and the discovery of a variety of dynamic symmetries in nuclei".<ref name=BonnerPrize/><ref>{{cite magazine |author=Llorens |first=Cecile Rivera |date=Summer 2011 |title=Rick Casten '63 Earns Top Physics Prize |url=https://magazine.holycross.edu/issue_45_3/45_3_alumni_spotlights/45_3_Casten |magazine=Holy Cross Magazine |publisher=[[College of the Holy Cross]] |volume=45 |issue=3 |access-date=November 27, 2023 |archive-date=November 28, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231128040811/https://magazine.holycross.edu/issue_45_3/45_3_alumni_spotlights/45_3_Casten |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=November 11, 2010 |title=Casten wins Bonner Prize in Nuclear Physics |url=https://news.yale.edu/2010/11/11/casten-wins-bonner-prize-nuclear-physics |access-date=2023-11-28 |website=YaleNews |publisher=[[Yale University]] |language=en}}</ref>
